title: Understanding ResNet
description: How residual connections solved the vanishing gradient problem.

body.raw:
Residual Networks (ResNets) introduce identity shortcuts so that layers learn residual functions.

## Why residuals help

Training very deep networks is hard because gradients vanish. Residual blocks learn
the difference between the input and the desired mapping:

$$ H(x) = F(x) + x $$

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

class BasicBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_ch, out_ch):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(in_ch, out_ch, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(out_ch, out_ch, 3, padding=1)
        )

    def forward(self, x):
        return torch.relu(self.net(x) + x)
```

The skip connection ensures gradients can flow directly to earlier layers.

title: Vision Transformers Explained
description: A breakdown of how ViTs process images as sequences.

body.raw:
Vision Transformers (ViTs) treat an image as a sequence of patches and apply
the Transformer encoder architecture.

## Patch embedding

Split an image into fixed-size patches and linearly project each to an embedding.

```python
import torch

def patchify(img, patch_size=16):
    b, c, h, w = img.shape
    ph = pw = patch_size
    img = img.view(b, c, h // ph, ph, w // pw, pw)
    return img.permute(0, 2, 4, 3, 5, 1).contiguous().view(b, -1, ph*pw*c)
```

## Self-attention

Each token attends to all others, capturing global context in a single layer.
